newsitem.title: UK: EBRD, Slovakia agree Slovnaft stake deal.
newsitem.headline: EBRD, Slovakia agree Slovnaft stake deal.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Slovakia's National Property Fund have reached an agreement under which the NPF will buy back the bank's stake in oil refiner Slovnaft a.s, officials said on Sunday.
The EBRD took a 10.5 percent stake in Slovnaft in 1995 when it bought half the refiner's $113 million issue of global depositary receipts, which flopped on international markets.

The bank later offered the shares for repurchase and agreement in principle was reached on Saturday in talks between EBRD president Jacques de Larosiere and Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik, Slovak officials said.

EBRD alternate director for Slovakia, Tomas Parizek, told a country presentation at the bank's annual meeting that the agreement would "allow the NPF to redeem the shares from the EBRD at a price which is acceptable to the EBRD".
He declined to give any details of the price.

When it bought the stake, the EBRD effectively paid the 1,000 crown face value per share. But shortly afterwards the NPF, Slovakia's privatisation agency, sold a 39 percent stake in the refiner to a management-led group at an implied price of just 156 crowns per share.
The EBRD has in the past expressed general concern at Slovakia's frequent practice of privatisation through management buyout, saying the sell-offs are usually well below market value.
The NPF holds 25 percent of Slovnaft, which was initially privatised in the first wave of mass voucher privatisation completed in 1993.
Slovnaft shares closed at 990 crowns each in Bratislava on Friday.
